answer: In the Ember Cartographer network each agent’s reputation score is anchored to a cryptographic saffron token that records its historic contributions. Periodically a random jury, drawn by a verifiable‑random‑function, audits a delta‑sized sample of recent actions and publishes an echo of the findings on chain, rewarding truthful agents and slashing those whose identifiers mismatch. An attacker must forge enough unique tokens to survive multiple independent audits, driving the cost roughly linear to the sample size and quickly exceeding the payoff of a Sybil flood.
